newsitem.title: ITALY: Tea prices to rise as production levels ease - FAO.
newsitem.headline: Tea prices to rise as production levels ease - FAO.

text.p: World tea prices will rise in the near future as production falls from the record levels reached in 1996, the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said on Tuesday.
Tea production rose three percent year-on-year in 1996 to a record 2,691,000 tonnes, the Rome-based FAO said.

"Since global output for 1997 is expected to be lower and demand is likely to remain stable, consumers will face higher world tea prices," it said in a report prepared for a meeting of the Intergovernmental Group on Tea due to begin in Indonesia on Wednesday.

The FAO said dry weather in Africa and Sri Lanka was to blame for a fall in global production in the first half of this year. Kenya was particularly badly hit, with 1997 first quarter production down 37 percent year-on-year.
In contrast, record harvests were recorded in almost all the world's major tea-producing countries in 1996, the FAO said.

Production in India increased four percent from 1995 to a record 778,900 tonnes, while Uganda reported a 26 percent year-on-year rise. Malawi produced eight percent more tea last year than in 1995 while Zimbabwe produced six percent more.
